current_allocator_cross_check.scope_note: This is a later live snapshot, so raw counts are not asserted as same-SHA equality. It is used together with source-code scope inspection to identify a routing-domain mismatch.

finding.summary: buildSnapshotFromRepo adds jobs from every root JSON file under coordination/opportunities by iterating each value.opportunities array. The fast allocator instead publishes only normalized feed projects plus currently ready plans. Consequently frontier-pressure can count repository-history opportunities as claimable even when they are not present in the current /wc routing surface. Those rows can suppress FRONTIER_THIN and inflate claimable/liveness metrics without giving workers a route to claim them.
code_evidence: scripts/compile-frontier-pressure.mjs: buildSnapshotFromRepo reads all root coordination/opportunities/*.json and pushes every value.opportunities row into jobs
.github/workflows/live-feed.yml: allocator ready/recovery derive from normalized feed projects and queue_ready derives from normalized current plans
finding.current_effect: The exact-snapshot compiler reports 80 claimable jobs while the nearby public allocator reports 0 ready + 0 queue_ready + 15 recovery. Because source SHAs differ, the magnitude is diagnostic rather than an equality assertion; the routing-domain mismatch itself is source-code deterministic.
finding.risk: If allocator-routable work falls below target while old queue-root rows remain nominally READY/replaceable, FRONTIER_THIN can remain false and fail to request replenishment despite a genuinely thin routable frontier.

truth_boundary: Verification/control-plane evidence only. No Current, Human Accepted, Served or production /w promotion.
